text:
elaine: quick check-in — profiler shows a ~18% tail-latency spike on PP bubble when microbatch=4. i think we're losing comm/compute overlap because of a kernel selection regression on A100s. attaching perf snippets below.

elaine: nvprof excerpt:
```
stage 0 compute: 1.8ms
stage 1 compute: 2.2ms
allreduce on stage boundary: 6.0ms (blocking)
stage 2 idle: 35% of step
KV cache refill: 0.9ms per token when miss
```

kyle: ouch. did you try forcing async progress / NCCL_COLL_ASYNC or NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR?

elaine: yep, NCCL_ASYNC=1 and NCCL_COLL_ASYNC=1 — no measurable improvement. allreduce still shows up as a blocking op in the trace. i also flipped our kernel-selector to prefer-fast-kernel=true and saw worse tail.

sam: what about kernel fallback? can you run with prefer-fast-kernel=false (force the compatibility slower kernels) to see if overlap improves?

elaine: ran that earlier today. results: prefer-fast-kernel=false => tail drops ~7% but aggregate token throughput drops ~4.5%. hypothesis: "fast" kernels are faster per-op but introduce synchronization points that prevent overlapping small allreduces across microbatches.

mike: any KV-cache signals? sometimes kvcache thrash can amplify idle windows if stages re-request kv pages mid-step.

elaine: good call. kvcache stats: microbatch=1 => KV hit 92%
microbatch=4 => KV hit 68% (we're seeing eviction spikes when we concatenate batches). pattern: when token lengths vary, we rebuild KV buffers which stalls stage transition.

elaine: snippet from kvcache log:
```
[KVCache] t=0: hit_count=9200 miss_count=800
[KVCache] t=1: hit_count=6800 miss_count=3200  <-- after MB=4 stress run
[KVCache] evictions=410, avg_refill=0.9ms
```

anna: suggestion: run a sweep with microbatch in {1,2,4}, chunk_size in {16,32}, prefer-fast-kernel in {true,false}, and a kvcache-capacity multiplier {1.0,1.5}. collect per-stage idle% and allreduce latency CDFs.

elaine: scheduling that now. i'll also enable continuous-batching heuristics off/on to see if our batching coalescer is causing large concatenations that thrash kv memory.

perf-bot: profiling job queued: pp-bubble-sampler-run-1767777777 — logs: https://ci.redwood/prof/1767777777 (will post when finished) :hourglass: 

kyle: when you have the profile, run the comm/compute overlap view (timeline) and attach the stacked bar per microbatch. we want to see if allreduces consistently align with frontier of compute or if they're clustered.

elaine: will do. next update in ~2 hours after the sweep finishes. initial takeaway: two interacting factors — kernel selection (fast kernel sync points) + kvcache thrash from larger microbatches — both contribute to PP bubble inefficiency. early mitigation: reduce microbatch to 2 + bump kvcache capacity 1.5x + prefer-fast-kernel=false gives a plausible perf sweet spot.

sam: good plan. also add a run with explicit interleaved allreduce scheduling (staggered by 1ms) to test if we can deconflict reductions in software schedule as a mitigation.

elaine: adding that. will post consolidated numbers + flamegraphs when available. :metal:
